narrative:
Isaias made landfall near Destin, FL, Friday evening. It has already weakened and is no longer a tropical storm. It moves north through Alabama and Tennessee today and will be in southeastern Kentucky early Sunday. From there the remnant low heads east.

Rain from Isaias arrived before sunrise and increases through the day. The heaviest rain falls this evening into early Sunday morning as feeder bands stream in from the Atlantic. Sunday morning the rain turns to showers, mostly on the west side of the Appalachians, and the showers end early Monday. Wind picks up this afternoon and stays with us through Monday.

Bottom lines:

Rain: 3 to 5 inches for most of the eastern half of the region, with locally higher amounts on the Blue Ridge and the highest terrain. Lesser amounts toward the NC/TN border.
Wind: gusts of 50 mph or more at higher elevations and around 40 mph in the valleys tonight into Sunday. Gusty winds remain Monday from the northwest.

Impacts: Stream flooding is likely, mostly in the eastern half of the mountain region. Expect some trees down and scattered power outages, especially tonight. It’s not Helene, but it is a significant storm nonetheless.

Forecast Discussion

Isaias came ashore at Destin, FL, as a Category 2 hurricane Friday evening. From there it weakened and is no longer a tropical storm. It moves north into Alabama and will continue a northerly track into southeastern Kentucky by early Sunday, then make a sharp turn east and be near the Delmarva early Monday morning. But the issue has never been the center of the system; rather it’s a potent stream of tropical moisture/energy being drawn into the system from the Atlantic and Gulf.

Rain arrived before sunrise in Western NC. Rain gradually increases through the day, and the feeder bands arrive this evening. Heaviest rain falls from this evening to early Sunday morning. Sunday morning a front associated with the Isaias remnant low moves through from the SW. Our weather turns showery, with most of the showers along the west side of the Appalachians. That ends early Monday morning. Below is one estimate of total rain for the event. Don’t take it literally, but it gives you the general idea--heaviest rain in the eastern half of the NC Mountain region, less rain along the western escarpment and north into Virginia.

Wind becomes an issue later today and windy conditions will be with us through Monday. Tonight into Sunday, expect ESE wind gusts of 50+ mph at higher elevations and 40ish in more populated areas. Monday will be a NW flow windy day.

Post-Isaias, high pressure centered in South Alabama takes control of our weather late Monday into early Wednesday. A front arrives from the northwest on Wednesday but is repelled northward on Thursday. Friday, another front moves through, allowing cooler air to settle into the region by next weekend. A shower is possible Thursday afternoon. Widely scattered showers are in play with the frontal passage Friday.
